title: W Chew, L Nibble: Chez Reggie
trend: TikTok 'W Chews / L Nibbles' (new slang rating food as a W chew or an L nibble, with a confused waiter reacting; trendhaus.ai TikTok list, first seen Nov 10 2026, US) — dad Reggie plays fancy waiter at a home dinner while his kids rate every course in slang he doesn't understand; twist: the toast reveals the meatloaf, potatoes and pie all came from the diner on Fifth Street (made by Linda), and the only thing Dad cooked was the sprouts that got an L nibble
youtube_title: Dad plays fancy waiter. The kids only speak in W chews and L nibbles 🍽️
description:
Reggie opens a fancy restaurant in the kitchen for one night. His kids rate every course in words he has never heard, and the toast knows where dinner really came from.

#cartoon #animation #funny #dinner #shorts

lines.text: Good evening, and welcome to Chez Reggie. Table for two critics.
Our first course tonight. Grandma's meatloaf, with a little glaze.
Mm. W chew.
Big W chew. Clean chew.
Is that good? Is that a grade? Is that a vitamin?
It's new lingo, Dad. You wouldn't get it.
I will write it down. Meatloaf. One W. Two chews.
He has been writing on a napkin since five o'clock.
Why is the toast in the restaurant?
I am the bread service. I have been here the whole time. Warmly.
Second course. Brussels sprouts, roasted with love and a lot of smoke.
L nibble.
Big L nibble. The sprout is giving cafeteria.
Giving what? Who is the sprout giving it to?
It's new lingo. You wouldn't get it.
I was cool once. I had a jacket with a lot of zippers.
The sprouts caught fire twice. I watched from the toaster.
That is called a char. Fancy places charge extra for a char.
Fine. Let me try the lingo. Ahem.
This bread service is a big W nibble.
No.
You cannot W a nibble. A nibble is always an L.
Please do not call me a nibble. I have a crust and a family.
Third course. Mashed potatoes. Very smooth. Zero chew.
Then how do we rate it?
Hmm. No chew. No nibble. It's a W slurp.
You are making these up now.
Dad. All words are made up. That is what words are.
I raised a philosopher. That is an L for my wallet.
See? He gets it now. That one was clean.
I get it! I am in! W chew, L nibble, big W slurp!
Okay. Do not say it at school pickup.
And for dessert, my famous homemade apple pie.
Homemade? The meatloaf was really good, Dad.
Yeah. Like, restaurant good. Suspicious good.
Should I tell them, or should you?
Tell them what? There is nothing to tell. Eat your pie.
The meatloaf came from the diner on Fifth Street. So did the potatoes.
Dad!
So did the pie. The sticker says, made with love by Linda.
So the only thing you actually cooked was the sprouts.
And the sprouts got an L nibble. From my own children.
Not the only thing. He also made me. I am homemade.
You came out of a bag, toast.
Every one of us came out of a bag, Milo.
Okay. Honest review. The meatloaf is a W chew for Linda.
The sprouts are an L nibble for Dad.
But Dad fighting a sprout fire for us? That is a big W.
A W what? A chew? A slurp?
Just a W, Dad. Plain W.
I will frame the napkin.
Tomorrow on the menu, cereal. Made by Linda.
Linda does not make cereal.
Not yet. I left her a note. On a napkin.
